results.title: An Evolutionary Perspective on Sports Nutrition: Strengths, Vulnerabilities, and Targeted Interventions in Homo sapiens
results.abstract: The genus Homo is characterized by several anatomic and physiologic traits that reflect millions of years of selection for sustained physical activity in hot environments. These adaptations include a high capacity for sweating, metabolic substrate flexibility during low-intensity activity, and several morphologic features of the lower limb and pelvis that facilitate energy-efficient locomotion. The present narrative review examines sports nutrition through an evolutionary lens by identifying the specific physiologic strengths and vulnerabilities of Homo sapiens and assessing the targeted nutritional interventions designed to address constraints on performance. Constraints discussed include submaximal resting phosphocreatine concentrations, modest proton-buffering capacity, limited rates of intestinal energy and carbohydrate (CHO) absorption, high water flux due to eccrine sweating, and an endurance-biased skeletal muscle phenotype that is not optimized for the accretion of large quantities of muscle tissue. Nutritional strategies reviewed include creatine monohydrate supplementation, supplements that increase muscle carnosine content, supplements that increase blood bicarbonate concentrations, exogenous CHO delivery, fluid and electrolyte replacement protocols, and high-protein dietary strategies to support hypertrophic adaptations to resistance training. Examining sports nutrition through an evolutionary lens facilitates assessment of the physiologic systems that frequently constrain exercise performance and the most viable nutritional strategies to mitigate these constraints.

results.title: Effects of high-intensity interval training versus continuous aerobic training on body weight, body mass index, and body fat percentage in youth with overweight or obesity: a systematic review and meta-analysis
results.abstract: Overweight and obesity in youth are associated with substantial short- and long-term health burdens, and structured exercise is a central component of management. Whether HIIT offers greater improvements in body composition than continuous aerobic training remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP were searched from inception to December 31, 2024 for randomized trials directly comparing high-intensity interval-based training, including high-intensity interval exercise and sprint-interval protocols, with continuous aerobic training in youth with overweight or obesity. Outcomes were body weight, BMI, and body fat percentage. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2. Random-effects models with REML estimation and modified Hartung-Knapp inference generated mean differences (MDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sensitivity, subgroup, and small-study-effect analyses were also performed. Fourteen independent randomized trials were included. For body weight, 13 trials involving 409 participants showed no statistically significant difference between HIIT and continuous aerobic training (MD = -0.37 kg, 95% CI -0.89 to 0.15; P = 0.146; I 2 = 0%). For BMI, 14 trials involving 432 participants also showed no significant difference (MD = -0.14 kg/m2, 95% CI -0.31 to 0.02; P = 0.089; I 2 = 0%). For body fat percentage, 11 trials involving 331 participants showed no significant difference (MD = -0.33 percentage points, 95% CI -1.33 to 0.67; P = 0.481), with moderate-to-substantial heterogeneity (I 2 = 60.3%). Sensitivity analyses did not materially alter the findings, and subgroup analyses did not identify reliable effect modification by weekly frequency, intervention duration, or mean age. Egger's tests did not detect statistically significant small-study effects. One trial was at low overall risk of bias, whereas 13 raised some concerns. Randomized evidence identified through December 31, 2024 does not show that HIIT provides greater reductions in body weight, BMI, or body fat percentage than continuous aerobic training. HIIT may be considered an alternative exercise format, but the limited evidence base and heterogeneity in body fat outcomes warrant cautious interpretation.

results.title: Effects of time-restricted eating on body composition and performance in athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
results.abstract: Time-restricted eating (TRE) has gained increasing attention as a dietary strategy for body mass management and metabolic health. However, its efficacy in athletic populations remains unclear. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to examine the effects of TRE on energy intake, body composition, and performance in athletes. Following PRISMA guidelines, the review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261291351). Six databases were searched from inception to January 10, 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing TRE with non-TRE dietary patterns in adult athletes were included if they reported body composition or performance outcomes. Pooled effects were estimated as standardized mean differences (SMDs; Hedges' g) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and evidence certainty using GRADE. Sixteen studies from 15 articles involving 245 athletes were included. TRE did not significantly alter energy intake (SMDpooled = -0.35, 95%CI: -0.77 to 0.07, p = 0.11). Compared with non-TRE dietary patterns, TRE resulted in small but significant reductions in body mass (SMDpooled = -0.27, 95%CI: -0.50 to -0.04; p = 0.02) and body fat% (SMDpooled = -0.39, 95%CI: -0.68 to -0.11, p = 0.01), while fat mass (SMDpooled = -0.23, 95%CI: -0.48 to 0.02, p = 0.07) and lean mass (SMDpooled = -0.16, 95%CI: -0.42 to 0.09, p = 0.21) were unchanged. TRE had no significant effects on aerobic capacity (SMDpooled = 0.04, 95%CI: -0.29 to 0.37, p = 0.82), muscular endurance (SMDpooled = -0.20, 95%CI: -0.52 to 0.13, p = 0.23), muscular strength (SMDpooled = 0.01, 95%CI: -0.25 to 0.27, p = 0.94), or power (SMDpooled = -0.12, 95%CI: -0.44 to 0.20, p = 0.47). Subgroup analyses suggested potentially greater reductions in body mass and body fat% among elite athletes, although between-subgroup differences were not statistically significant. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. TRE may represent a feasible dietary strategy for athletes seeking modest reductions in body mass and body fat% without clear detrimental effects on performance. However, evidence remains limited by small samples, short interventions, and methodological concerns, warranting larger, well-controlled, and longer-term trials across diverse athletic populations. PROSPERO unique identifier CRD420261291351.

results.title: Glycation proteomics identifies creatine kinase as a mediator of the effects of methylglyoxal on mitochondrial permeability transition
results.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
results.abstract: Opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition (PT) pore is an important step in necrotic cell death in various pathologic conditions such as ischemia-reperfusion injury. Methylglyoxal (MGO) is a byproduct of glycolysis that covalently modifies proteins (i.e., glycation) and is widely regarded as toxic (glycative stress), contributing to the pathology of diabetes. Paradoxically, MGO has been shown to inhibit PT pore opening, but the mechanism of this effect is poorly understood. Herein we show that glycation is elevated in various cardioprotective scenarios. Furthermore, building on a serendipitous finding of the ability of phosphate to block MGO's effect on the PT pore, we used proteomics to map potential sites mediating this effect. From this analysis, mitochondrial creatine kinase (CK) emerged as a phosphate-sensitive MGO target with links to the PT pore. Although MGO inhibited CK activity, this did not appear to be important for its effect on the PT pore. Rather, MGO modified sites on CK that are important for its membrane binding, which likely mediates the combined effects of MGO and phosphate on the PT pore. Furthermore, a consensus sequence for MGO modifications in mitochondria is reported.

results.title: Aerobic exercise, whey protein, and creatine in adolescents: implications for performance, recovery, immunometabolic adaptation, and muscle-bone-brain crosstalk
results.abstract: Adolescence constitutes a pivotal developmental phase for the enhancement of musculoskeletal and metabolic wellbeing, as well as neurodevelopment, during which specific exercise regimens and nutritional interventions can precipitate enduring physiological transformations. Although aerobic exercise has conventionally been linked to enhancements in cardiovascular fitness and metabolic control, the confluence of this form of exercise with anabolic and ergogenic supplements, including whey protein and creatine, in adolescent populations has not been extensively investigated. This narrative review examines current evidence on aerobic exercise, whey protein, and creatine in adolescents, with particular emphasis on exercise performance, recovery, immunometabolic adaptation, and muscle-bone-brain crosstalk. A narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar using combinations of terms related to aerobic exercise, whey protein, creatine, adolescents, exercise performance, recovery, immunometabolism, and muscle-bone-brain signaling. Relevant peer-reviewed studies published from database inception to May 2026 were considered, with emphasis on adolescent human studies and selected mechanistic evidence from experimental and adult populations when directly relevant to biological interpretation. Aerobic exercise promotes oxidative metabolic processes, mitochondrial functionality, and endurance performance, thereby enhancing mitochondrial biogenesis and metabolic flexibility. Whey protein supplies critical amino acids that incite muscle protein turnover and modulate pivotal signaling cascades, thereby supporting muscle remodeling and recovery. Creatine, in addition to its function in the swift regeneration of adenosine triphosphate, plays a significant role in cellular hydration, the preservation of mitochondrial integrity, and the maintenance of antioxidant defense mechanisms, while also potentially influencing brain energy metabolism and brain-derived neurotrophic factor-mediated neuroplasticity. Emerging evidence further suggests that exercise and nutritional interventions may influence inflammatory mediators, myokines, osteokines, and neurotrophic pathways involved in muscle-bone-brain communication. However, mechanistic evidence is frequently derived from animal or non-adolescent human studies, and direct evidence for combined interventions in adolescents remains limited. Overall, aerobic exercise, whey protein, and creatine may have complementary roles in supporting exercise performance, recovery, and metabolic adaptation during adolescence, although further well-controlled adolescent studies are needed to establish their long-term efficacy, safety, and optimal use.

results.title: Sitting posture influence on the biomechanical responses of the seated human body to whole-body vibration
results.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers. Part H, Journal of engineering in medicine
results.abstract: Whole-body vibration (WBV) is widely used in rehabilitation, clinical practice and sports to improve various health conditions and enhance muscle performance. However, the biomechanical mechanisms underlying these beneficial effects remain unclear. Although vibration transmission during WBV training has been investigated in standing postures, seated postures remain largely unexplored. This study investigated how three sitting postures (slouched, upright, and tense) affect vibration transmission to and through the human body during WBV exposure. Twelve healthy male participants were exposed to vertical sinusoidal vibration with amplitude of 14.3 m/s2 and frequency of 30 Hz while seated on a force plate mounted on the vibrating platform of a WBV training machine. Vertical and fore-and-aft head accelerations and interface forces between the body and the vibrating platform were measured. The tense posture produced significantly greater vertical and fore-and-aft head accelerations than the slouched and upright postures, indicating increased vibration transmissibility to the head with upper-body stiffening. In contrast, interface forces did not differ significantly among postures. It was concluded that sitting posture influences vibration transmission to the head during WBV exposure, whereas its effect on interface forces appears limited. A tense sitting posture increases head vibration transmissibility, emphasising the importance of posture when designing safe and effective WBV interventions.

results.title: Effects of high-intensity interval training on body composition, cardiorespiratory fitness, and selected lipid outcomes in adult women with overweight or obesity: a systematic review and meta-analysis
results.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on body composition, cardiorespiratory fitness, and selected lipid outcomes in adult women with overweight, obesity, or normal-weight obesity. This review followed the PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261394616). PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Embase, and MEDLINE via Ovid were searched from database inception to 26 July 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials involving adult women with overweight, obesity, or normal-weight obesity and comparing HIIT with control conditions without structured exercise. Outcomes included body weight (BW), body mass index (BMI), body fat percentage (BF%), fat mass (FM), maximal or peak oxygen uptake (VO2max/VO2peak), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), total cholesterol (TC), and triglycerides (TG). Hedges' g with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) was used as the pooled effect measure, and random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Fifteen randomized controlled trials were included. Compared with controls without structured exercise, HIIT significantly reduced BW (g = -0.33, 95% CI -0.58 to -0.08; P = 0.01), BMI (g = -0.56, 95% CI -0.95 to -0.17; P< 0.01), BF% (g = -0.76, 95% CI -1.35 to -0.17; P = 0.01), and FM (g = -0.66, 95% CI -1.11 to -0.20; P< 0.01), and significantly improved VO2max/VO2peak (g = 1.09, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.47; P< 0.01). HIIT also increased HDL-C and reduced LDL-C, whereas effects on TC and TG were not statistically significant. Subgroup and meta-regression analyses were exploratory. Evidence certainty ranged from low to very low. Current randomized evidence suggests that, compared with controls without structured exercise, HIIT may favor adiposity-related body-composition outcomes and cardiorespiratory fitness in adult women with overweight, obesity, or normal-weight obesity, whereas its effects on selected lipid outcomes remain uncertain. The review did not systematically evaluate other cardiometabolic outcomes, including blood pressure, insulin resistance, glycemic control, or inflammatory markers. The findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of studies, small sample sizes, between-study heterogeneity, and low to very low certainty of evidence. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261394616.

results.title: Liposomal and Polymeric Drug Delivery of Creatine: Exploring a Multifaceted Molecule for Neurodegenerative Diseases and Beyond
results.abstract: Creatine (Cr), best known as a sports supplement, is increasingly recognized for its multifaceted biological functions and broad therapeutic potential. Through its roles in cellular energy homeostasis, mitochondrial function, oxidative stress reduction, and neuroinflammation modulation, Cr has shown therapeutic potential in neurodegenerative diseases (NDs), cancer, and other disorders of energy metabolism. For NDs specifically, the application of Cr may be hindered by poor bioavailability, high dose requirements, and, most importantly, its limited ability to efficiently cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Advances in nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems have introduced new approaches that may help address these limitations by improving pharmacokinetics, facilitating BBB penetration, enabling targeted drug delivery, and supporting controlled drug release. Among these platforms, liposomes and polymer-based systems have been widely studied because of their favorable biocompatibility, safety profiles, and translational potential. These delivery strategies have mainly been evaluated in preclinical studies and in models of diseases other than NDs. This review examines the therapeutic potential of Cr in NDs by integrating current knowledge of its biological functions with developments in liposomal and polymeric drug delivery systems that may facilitate brain delivery and improve therapeutic outcomes. Recent studies of Cr-based formulations, Cr analogues, phosphocreatine, and other nanocarrier systems have provided insights into different approaches for improving Cr delivery and expanding its therapeutic applications. Furthermore, it summarizes recent progress in Cr-based nanomedicine, identifies current translational challenges, and highlights future research directions to advance Cr-based therapies, particularly for NDs, with potential applications in cancer and other energy metabolism-related disorders.

results.title: Protonation- and substrate-regulated dimer opening couples brain-type creatine kinase to vesicular and actin-remodeling membranes
results.abstract: Brain-type creatine kinase (CK-BB) buffers local ATP demand through reversible phosphotransfer between ATP and phosphocreatine, yet how this soluble metabolic enzyme couples to dynamic membrane compartments remains unclear. Here, we integrate immunofluorescence microscopy, DEER spectroscopy, hydrogen-deuterium exchange and native mass spectrometry, DEER- and AlphaFold-guided modeling, and long-timescale molecular dynamics to define the acid- and substrate-regulated conformational landscape of human CK-BB. Acidification redistributes endogenous and recombinant CK-BB from a diffuse cytosolic pool to punctate vesicular structures and membrane ruffles. DEER and modeling reveal a spatially asymmetric dimer in which the convex surface remains comparatively restrained, whereas the concave catalytic-regulatory surface samples pH- and substrate-dependent conformational intermediates. We identify progressive dimer opening as a novel regulatory mechanism by which acidic pH and substrate binding increase dynamics across the convex surface and NTD-NTD interface and sensitize the His191/Ser199 module to graded pH-dependent exchange. Substrate binding buffers acid-induced deprotection while preserving localized dynamics near this regulatory interface. Together, these data support a model in which protonation and substrate occupancy generate membrane-competent CK-BB conformations, coupling local ATP regeneration to curved vesicular and actin-remodeling membranes.

results.title: Adverse effects of vaping on human health: a brief review of mechanisms and long-term consequences
results.journal: Arhiv za higijenu rada i toksikologiju
results.abstract: Vaping, often advertised as a safe alternative to traditional tobacco smoking, has recently been subjected to active scientific research due to its potential adverse effects on human health. This narrative review synthesises selected recent literature to provide a comprehensive view of the systemic risks associated with the use of electronic cigarettes. It lists key chemical components (propylene glycol, vegetable glycerine, nicotine, and flavourings) and thermal decomposition products of vape aerosol (formaldehyde, acrolein, propylene oxide, glycidol) and evaluates their multi-systemic toxic effects and clinical manifestations, as well as specific effects on the respiratory, cardiovascular, immune, and nervous systems. Current data suggest that vaping can lead to a wide range of acute and chronic diseases, including the e-cigarette or vaping-associated lung injury (EVALI) and obliterative bronchiolitis and increase the risk of developing oncological, cardiovascular, and neurological diseases. Particularly sensitive is the developing adolescent brain. A growing body of evidence indicates that vaping is not "less harmful" but merely "differently" harmful and calls for further long-term research and strengthened public health regulation.

results.title: Effects of Tabata-style functional training and cinnamon supplementation on army combat fitness test performance, serum irisin, and body composition in military cadets: a randomized controlled trial
results.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
results.abstract: The study aimed to assess the effect of Tabata-style functional training with or without cinnamon supplementation on the performance of the Army Combat Fitness Test (ACFT), serum irisin levels, and body composition in cadets at military academies. In a randomized controlled design, 48 male cadets (22.8 ± 1.3 years) were allocated to 4 groups: Tabata group (n = 14), cinnamon group (n = 10), Tabata+cinnamon (n = 14), and control group (n = 10). This was a 6-week intervention. Tabata training was performed three times per week (8 × 20s work/10s rest; 87%-95% HRmax), and cinnamon (Cinnamomum zeylanicum) supplementation was administered three times per day (1.5g per day). The ACFT components, serum irisin, body fat percentage (BFP), visceral fat index (VFI), lean body mass (LBM), and body mass index (BMI) were evaluated before and after treatment. The group × time interaction was significant for ACFT score, irisin, and body composition markers (p < 0.001). Bonferroni post hoc showed that ACFT test scores in both groups, COMB and TAB, improved significantly compared to the CON group (p < 0.05). Significant improvement was observed for groups COMB and TAB in 3 repetition maximum Deadlift, Standing Power Throw, Release Pushups, Sprint-Drag-Carry, Leg Tuck, and 2-Mile Run compared to CON group (p < 0.05). The most significant increase in serum irisin levels was observed in COMB group compared to the other groups (p < 0.001). All groups showed significant reductions in body weight, BMI, and VFI when compared to the control group (p < 0.05). Among the groups, TAB group had a remarkably lower BFP than the others (p < 0.001). Additionally, LBM increased significantly in all groups compared to the control group (p < 0.001). Tabata-style training combined with cinnamon supplementation markedly enhanced performance, body composition, and circulating irisin in young male military cadets, yielding significant improvements in functional capacity and demonstrating the advantage of pairing high-intensity exercise with targeted nutritional intervention.

results.title: The effect of spatial bottleneck on human eco-cultural range expansion
results.journal: Journal of the Royal Society, Interface
results.abstract: The spatial spread of humans and culture is shaped by feedback between demography and cultural accumulation, as captured by the eco-cultural range expansion model. Yet, the effect of geographical boundaries on this process remains poorly understood. Here, we extend the model to a two-dimensional space where two large habitats are connected by a narrow corridor (spatial bottleneck) with reflecting boundaries. We find that a wave of ecological invasion always passes the bottleneck, whereas the subsequent transition to a high-density/high-culture equilibrium can be blocked by sufficiently narrow corridors. The maximum bottleneck width that prevents propagation depends on the domain shape, and it converges to the threshold value when the habitat to be invaded gets larger. Our results align with mathematical results on a bistable reaction- diffusion equation, particularly mean curvature flow, based on which we provide an approximate formula for the threshold bottleneck width. Applied to the Middle-Upper Palaeolithic transition, the findings suggest that while the spread of modern humans was robust to spatial bottlenecks, the expansion of advanced Upper Palaeolithic culture could be delayed or halted by narrow corridors. Archaeological records point to potential cases where such geographic bottlenecks constrained cultural dispersal.

results.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of phospholipids in human milk
results.abstract: Phospholipids are important bioactive components in human milk. They are rich in unsaturated fatty acids and play crucial roles in cell signal transduction and infant intellectual development. This study quantitatively pooled concentrations of total phospholipids and their subclasses in human milk, and narratively summarized phospholipid subclass proportions across different countries. Relevant studies published up to October 2025 were searched from six databases. After systematic search, a total of 25 studies were finally included, among which 18 studies on phospholipid concentrations were subjected to meta-analysis. Results from the random-effects model showed that the total phospholipid concentration was 251.60 mg/L (175.62, 327.58) in colostrum, 234.71 mg/L (171.07, 298.35) in transitional milk, 197.00 mg/L (166.08, 227.93) in mature milk. Throughout lactation, PC, SM, and PE are the major phospholipid classes in human milk. Subgroup meta-analyses indicated that detection methods were a significant effect for total phospholipids, PE, and PI concentrations within mature milk. This systematic review provides updated estimates of phospholipids and their subclasses concentrations in term human milk, and provides a theoretical basis for the application of phospholipids in infant formula. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, Identiffer CRD420261445346.

results.title: Partial Immersion Using Body Bags for Exertional Hyperthermia: A Randomized Crossover Study
results.journal: The western journal of emergency medicine
results.abstract: Recent recommendations suggest emergency medical personnel should consider rapid whole-body cooling for heat stroke patients. Cold-water immersion maximizes cooling rate and subsequent outcomes following heat stroke. Body bags filled with ice and water may provide portable, accessible partial cold-water immersion for this setting. The purpose of this study was to determine whole-body cooling rates when using body bags to facilitate partial cold-water immersion to treat exertional hyperthermia. A total of 9 healthy participants (8 male; mean [SD] age, 24 [4] years; height, 175 [7] cm; body mass, 83.6 [21.6] kg) completed our randomized-crossover field study. Following hydration verification, participants completed a self-paced 400 warm-up run, 1,609 m run, and 10-m sprints until rectal temperature (T-rec) reached 39.2 °C or volitional exhaustion. Following exercise, participants were cooled for a maximum of 30 minutes lying supine in the shade (control; CON) or in body bags filled with 20 gallons of ice water (5.2 [1.6] °C). Following cooling, participants sat upright for a 15-minute recovery. T-rec and heart rate (HR) were taken throughout exercise, every minute of cooling, and every 5 minutes of recovery. Participants completed both trials separated by 1 week in random order. Wet bulb globe temperature between trials was not significantly different (grand mean, 28.43 [1.03] °C; P = .73). There was no difference in participant maximum T-rec (body bag, 38.98 [.23] °C; CON, 38.93 [.39] °C; P = .45); HR (body bag, 183 [14] beats per minute [bpm]; CON, 189 [13] bpm; P = .21); rating of perceived exertion (P >.99); thirst (P = .62); or thermal sensation (P = .73) during exercise. Fluid consumed (P = .40), body mass change (P = .90), 400 m run times (P = .19) and 1,609 m run times (P = .17) were no different between trials. Whole-body cooling rate for body bag was .102 (.04) °C/min, whereas CON produced a cooling rate of .040 (.04) °C/min (95% CI, .030-.095; P = .002). Total cooling time was significantly faster (13.2 (5.8) min) with BB compared to CON (27.6 (4.2) min; 95% CI, 9.2-19.5; P = .002). In clinical settings where full-body cold-water immersion is not feasible, or during emergency transport, partial immersion via body bags offers acceptable cooling rates for hyperthermic patients. Emergency medical personnel could apply these data for support in updating heat stroke protocols to include partial immersion via body bag during transport, or immediately upon emergency department arrival.

results.title: Effectiveness of a digital weight management program on weight-bias internalization, self-compassion, quality of life, well-being, and body appreciation: secondary outcomes from a randomized controlled trial
results.journal: Annals of behavioral medicine : a publication of the Society of Behavioral Medicine
results.abstract: While evidence suggests psychosocial support benefits well-being, physical health, and weight management, the impact of psychosocial health within digital behavioral weight management programs (compared to traditional in-person models) remains underexplored. To evaluate the effectiveness of a digital commercial program (DCP) compared to standard nutrition guidance (SNG) on some weight-related psychosocial outcomes: weight-bias internalization (WBI), self-compassion, weight-related quality of life (WQOL), well-being, and body appreciation (BA). A 6-month randomized controlled trial (NCT05648344) was conducted among 376 US adults living with overweight/obesity. n = 187 were randomized to a DCP (WeightWatchers®), and n = 189 received SNG. Intention-to-treat analyses using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusted for sex, age, race, ethnicity, education, body mass index (BMI), and baseline values, were completed to assess changes in outcomes. Mean ± SD age was 47.7 ± 12.2 years; 7.4% self-identified as Asian; 13.8% Black; 6.4% Other; 9.6% Hispanic; 20.7% male; 17.8% experienced food insecurity; BMI = 33.6 ± 4.7 kg/m2. At 6 months, DCP relative to SNG, participants lowered their WBI by a mean difference ± SE of -0.3 ± 0.1; and increased their self-compassion by 0.2 ± 0.1; BA by 0.2 ± 0.1; well-being by 6.4 ± 1.7, and WQOL by 5.6 ± 1.2, all P<.01. Relative to SNG, participants in the DCP showed increased self-compassion, BA, well-being, and WQOL, and decreased WBI, highlighting that DCPs may deliver favorable changes in psychosocial outcomes. These findings should be interpreted with caution due to the short follow-up period and the question of whether the observed differences are clinically meaningful.

results.title: "Ozempic Face" and Facial Aging
results.abstract: The widespread adoption of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists has introduced a growing clinical challenge for dermatologists and cosmetic practitioners: managing the facial changes associated with rapid weight loss. The term "Ozempic face" has entered popular vocabulary to describe the appearance of accelerated facial aging in patients on these medications, characterized by volume deflation, skin laxity, and loss of structural support. This review examines the anatomical and histological basis of these changes, with attention to the roles of dermal white adipose tissue (dWAT), skeletal remodeling, and sarcopenia. We discuss the clinical presentation of weight-loss-associated facial change and outline a practical framework for patient assessment and counseling. The timing and sequencing of interventions across the weight loss journey are addressed, with emphasis on a health-first approach that prioritizes tissue preservation. As GLP-1 receptor agonists expand into new therapeutic indications, including inflammatory skin diseases, dermatology clinicians are uniquely positioned to counsel and manage patients experiencing these changes.

results.title: Effect of web-based education on NIV-related side effects and insomnia severity in COPD patients using home NIV: a randomized controlled trial
results.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of web-based education on NIV-related side effects and insomnia severity in COPD patients using home noninvasive ventilation (NIV). This randomized controlled trial was conducted with 75 patients between October 2023 and May 2024. Data were collected using the S³-NIV Questionnaire and the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI). The intervention group received web-based education regarding NIV-related side effects and insomnia management. Independent samples t-tests were used to compare numerical descriptive characteristics between groups, while Pearson chi-square and Fisher's exact tests were used for categorical variables. Repeated-measures ANOVA was performed to evaluate changes over time and between groups. Compared with the control group, the intervention group demonstrated significantly higher total S³-NIV Questionnaire scores and higher respiration, sleep, and side-effect subscale scores at weeks 4 and 8. Significant group × time interaction effects were observed for total S³-NIV scores (p < 0.001, η²p = 0.753) and ISI scores (p < 0.001, η²p = 0.352). For insomnia severity, no significant between-group difference in ISI scores was observed at Week 4, whereas ISI scores were significantly lower in the intervention group at Week 8. Web-based education may help improve patient-reported NIV-related symptoms and reduce insomnia severity in patients with COPD using home NIV. These findings suggest that web-based educational interventions may support symptom management and patient adaptation in clinical practice.

results.title: Dose-related cardiac side effects and its impact on survival following thoracic radiotherapy: A scoping review
results.abstract: Radiation dose to the heart is associated with various cardiac side effects. However, the specific cardiac and pulmonary structures that contribute to these toxicities remain incompletely understood. Moreover, although multiple factors contribute to reduced survival after radiotherapy, the role of radiation-induced cardiac toxicity remains underrecognized. This scoping review aimed to evaluate the associations between radiation dose to specific cardiac and pulmonary structures, cardiac side effects, and survival. A total of 137 clinical studies were analysed in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Associations between radiation dose and cardiac side effects were identified not only for the whole heart but also for specific cardiac substructures, including myocardial segments, coronary arteries, and the pericardium. Notably, radiation dose to the lungs was also associated with decline in cardiac function, suggesting that minimizing cardiac toxicity may require consideration of both local cardiac irradiation and non-local irradiation of adjacent organs, particularly the lungs. Direct evidence linking cardiac side effects to survival was limited. Nevertheless, the observed associations between higher radiation doses, increased cardiac toxicity, and poorer survival suggest a potential relationship that warrants further investigation. These findings support the hypothesis that reducing specific cardiac side effects may benefit from targeted sparing of the relevant cardiac and pulmonary substructures. While many radiation-related cardiac side effects are now recognized, further research is needed to identify and characterize previously unrecognized manifestations and to clarify their contribution to long-term survival.

results.title: Interrogating side effects: The role of social information in treatment expectancies
results.abstract: Negative expectancies play a key role in the symptoms people experience. Recent research has identified social information, such as media reports and written anecdotes, as capable of producing negative expectancies and subsequent symptoms. With the increasing availability of anecdotal health information online, and the increasing use of online sources in health or treatment-related decision making, this is a key concern. However, present literature on socially induced expectancy formation passively presents specific information to participants. In an online context, individuals actively choose to engage with certain types of information. The current studies were thus designed to investigate (a) what type of treatment information people typically engage with, when presented with positive and negative information, and (b) whether the type of information one selects relates to their subsequent treatment expectancies. Across three online studies, participants were presented with an information leaflet describing a medication and were then asked to select to read a number of anecdotes describing either positive or negative experiences of side effects associated with the treatment. Across the three studies, people selected relatively more negative than positive anecdotes. People who selected more negative anecdotes also had greater expectancies for side effects and worry about side effects. There was moderate evidence that selecting more negative anecdotes also decreased willingness to try the treatment. These results demonstrate that accounting for the type of information people tend to interrogate is crucial to understanding treatment expectancies and decisions, and suggest that valenced interrogation bias may represent an important cognitive mechanism contributing negative expectancies.
mesh: Drug-Related Side Effects and Adverse Reactions

results.title: Single-item measures of perceived side effect burden for people with cancer: A systematic scoping review
results.abstract: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) recommends the use of single-item measures in cancer clinical trials to capture patients' global perceptions of treatment-related side effect burden. This systematic scoping review aimed to summarise the (1) use of single-item measures in published studies and registered clinical trials, and (2) psychometric and content-related evidence for two items highlighted by the FDA: EORTC item Q168 and FACIT item GP5. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and PsycINFO were searched alongside major clinical trial registries. Eligible records included studies and trials involving people with cancer that used or evaluated single-item measures of perceived side effect burden. Data were summarised narratively to describe patterns of use, psychometric, and content-related evidence. The search yielded 2395 unique records. Following screening, 67 published studies and 74 clinical trial records were included. In published studies, EORTC item Q168 remains concentrated within pancreatic and biliary cancer settings, whereas clinical trials registrations suggest increasing use in other cancer types; meanwhile, FACIT item GP5 has been used across various study designs and cancer types. Published studies reported findings related to content, convergent, and known-groups validity, reliability, and responsiveness, most of which related to FACIT item GP5 (n = 27), with substantially fewer studies examining EORTC item Q168 (n = 2). However, important conceptual limitations remain, particularly regarding the inherent difficulty of attributing symptoms to treatment rather than to disease or other factors. Single-item measures may be pragmatic indicators of perceived treatment-related side effect burden; particularly where minimising respondent burden is important. However, further research is needed to strengthen evidence regarding content validity, measurement properties, and their added value alongside multidimensional patient-reported outcome measures.

results.title: Effect of galactose side-chain modification on immunomodulatory activity of tamarind xyloglucan oligosaccharides
results.abstract: Xyloglucan, an abundant polysaccharide bearing galactose side-chains within the cell wall of cotyledons from leguminous seeds, exhibits superior immunomodulatory properties. However, the contribution of its galactose side-chains remains unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the role of the galactose side-chains in the immunomodulatory activity by comparing the effects of oligosaccharides with different degrees of galactosyl substitution on RAW 264.7 mouse macrophages. Three structurally distinct xyloglucan fractions were prepared from tamarind seed: native high-molecular-weight xyloglucan (XG), low-molecular-weight xyloglucan oligosaccharides (XGOS) and partially degalactosylated XGOS (De-XGOS). All three components effectively promote macrophage proliferation and activation. Compared with De-XGOS, XGOS, which retained more galactose side-chains, generally exhibited stronger immunomodulatory responses in several functional assays. Furthermore, by stimulating the activation of the TLR4 signaling pathway, it triggered the expression of NF-κB pathway proteins, thereby elevating reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels to 1.71-fold and promoting the secretion of cytokines such as IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α. Pretreatment with the TLR4 inhibitor TAK-242 significantly attenuated XGOS-induced NO and TNF-α production, supporting the involvement of TLR4 signaling in macrophage activation. Molecular docking further suggested potential interactions between representative xyloglucan oligosaccharide structures and TLR4/MD2. In addition, the conditioned medium from XGOS-treated macrophages inhibited 4 T1 breast cancer cell migration and invasion by 38.90% and 33.33%, respectively. This study provides mechanistic insights into the structure-function relationship of xyloglucan oligosaccharides and suggests that galactose side-chain retention may contribute to their immunomodulatory activity.

results.title: Social media use and expectations predict COVID-19 vaccine side effects: a prospective longitudinal study
results.abstract: Social media use has been implicated in the development of anti-vaccine attitudes. However, its connection with the post-vaccination experience itself remains unclear. The present longitudinal study examined how expectations and psychosocial factors are associated with the relationship between exposure to reports of COVID-19 vaccine side effects on social media and observers' post-vaccination side effect experience. Prospective longitudinal study using online surveys. Five hundred thirty-eight adults residing in Australia indicated the burden (i.e., number of symptoms and related severity) of COVID-19 vaccine side effects seen reported by other users on social media and their own expectations of experiencing post-vaccination side effects (T1). Perceptions of social media and psychosocial beliefs were also measured. Experience of vaccine-attributed side effects were self-reported after participants received their first (T2; n = 299) and second (T3; n = 155) vaccine doses. There was a significant positive association between social media side effect burden exposure and the side effect burden experienced after receiving the first dose. Pre-vaccination side effect expectations formed an indirect association between these variables, but not for the exposure-second dose association. Worry about COVID-19 vaccine side effects, greater side effect severity experienced by known others, and stronger vaccine misconceptions strengthened the first dose indirect association through expectations. Exposure to user-posted health information on social media was positively associated with post-vaccination side effect experiences and the pre-vaccination expectations associated with this relationship were modulated by several psychosocial factors. Health interventions should consider the potential role of social media-derived symptom information on negative health outcomes.

results.title: Indigenous Knowledge and Food-Based Coping Mechanisms for ART Side Effects: A Qualitative Inquiry
results.abstract: Sustained adherence to antiretroviral therapy (ART) is critical for managing HIV, yet side effects and food insecurity present significant barriers in resource-limited settings. While the role of formal support is recognized, the use of indigenous knowledge and food-based coping mechanisms remains an underdocumented facet of self-management. This study explored how individuals in Ghana utilize local foods and cultural knowledge to manage ART side effects and support adherence. A qualitative descriptive study was conducted at the Cape Coast Teaching Hospital. Through semistructured in-depth interviews (n = 20) and one focus group discussion (n = 5) with adults on ART for at least 6 months, we collected rich, experiential data. Participants were purposively sampled, and data collection continued until thematic saturation was achieved. Thematic analysis was employed to identify patterns and themes related to food-based coping strategies. Analysis revealed that participants strategically employed indigenous knowledge, using specific local foods as active agents to manage side effects. Ginger tea was used to combat nausea, while avocado and groundnuts served as a protective stomach buffer. The timing of medication was often deliberately aligned with meals, with participants delaying doses if food was unavailable to avoid distress. These practices were deeply pragmatic, relying on affordable staples like gari (cassava flour) and yams, and were seamlessly integrated into daily routines. While these strategies demonstrated significant patient agency and resilience, they were also born from necessity, often representing suboptimal adaptations to food insecurity and poverty. Indigenous knowledge provides a crucial, culturally resonant toolkit for managing ART side effects and facilitating adherence. Healthcare systems should move beyond generic instructions to formally recognize, validate, and integrate these patient-derived strategies into adherence counseling and peer support, fostering a more holistic and effective model of HIV care that bridges biomedical and indigenous knowledge systems.

results.title: Gastrointestinal Side Effects of Low-Dose Oral Minoxidil in Patients with Alopecia: An Underrecognized Association
results.abstract: Low-dose oral minoxidil (LDOM) has become an increasingly used therapy for alopecia. While dose-dependent hypertrichosis is the most common side effect, gastrointestinal (GI) adverse effects are plausible due to smooth muscle relaxation, but they have not been systematically reported in clinical studies. To investigate the frequency and characteristics of GI adverse effects in patients treated with LDOM for alopecia. We conducted a prospective observational study at a trichology unit including patients attending their second consultation after initiating oral minoxidil between May and August 2025. A structured questionnaire assessed new GI symptoms, temporal relationship with treatment, and concomitant medication use. Among 302 patients (218 females, 84 males; mean age 46 years), 22 (7.3%) reported new GI symptoms. The most frequent symptoms were flatulence (N=18), heartburn (N=13), abdominal distension (N=12), abdominal pain (N=10), and aerophagia (N=7). Symptoms resolved after discontinuation in 15 of 16 cases and recurred after reintroduction in 14 of 15. A dose-response association was observed (mean dose in patients with GI symptoms 2.7 ± 1.6 mg vs. 1.3 ± 1.2 mg in those without, P=0.01). GI side effects were more common in males (15.5%) than in females (4.1%, P<0.001) and in patients treated with concomitant vasodilators (25.6% vs. 4.6%, P<0.001). GI complaints, particularly aerophagia, abdominal pain or distension, and flatulence, appear to be underrecognized adverse effects of LDOM. Although generally mild, these symptoms may affect adherence and quality of life. Clinicians should inquire about GI complaints, especially in male patients receiving higher doses or concomitant vasodilators.

results.title: Hemispheric Contributions to Figurative Language Comprehension After Unilateral Brain Damage: A Meta-Analysis of Lesion Side and Conventionality Interaction
results.abstract: Previous studies revealed that individuals with brain damage exhibit distinctive patterns in figurative language comprehension. However, a systematic investigation of the mechanisms between figurative language deficits and moderating factors such as lesion side remains lacking. Moreover, while the right hemisphere has traditionally been emphasized in pragmatic processing, accumulating evidence now suggests that the contributions of the left and right hemispheres may depend on linguistic factors such as conventionality. A recent systematic review on idiom comprehension in aphasia has highlighted the critical role of stimulus characteristics, yet no quantitative synthesis has examined how conventionality modulates hemispheric contributions to figurative language processing after unilateral brain damage. This meta-analysis aims to: (1) quantify the overall difference between left- and right-hemisphere damaged (LBD and RBD) patients in figurative language comprehension accuracy; (2) examine whether conventionality moderates hemispheric differences; (3) explore potential moderators-including aphasia status, task type, and sample size-that may influence the LBD-RBD difference; and (4) compare impairment patterns of LBD and RBD patients relative to healthy controls across different conventionality levels. Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature search was conducted across Web of Science, PubMed, and ProQuest. Studies comparing LBD and/or RBD patients to healthy controls on accuracy in figurative language comprehension tasks were included. Multi-level meta-analyses were performed to estimate overall effect sizes, examine moderating effects of conventionality, and compare impairment patterns. Meta-regressions explored potential moderators including aphasia status, sample size, task types, and number of trials. Forty-five articles met inclusion criteria, with 13 articles providing direct LBD-RBD comparisons (516 LBD; 476 RBD patients). Overall, no significant main effect of hemisphere emerged. Although the interaction between conventionality and lesion side did not reach statistical significance, the pattern of effect sizes across conventionality levels revealed meaningful trends. At high conventionality, LBD patients showed greater deficits than RBD patients, while at low conventionality, RBD patients showed greater deficits. Moderator analyses further revealed that task type and sample size significantly modulated the overall LBD-RBD difference, whereas aphasia status and number of trials did not. Additional comparisons including 70 LBD versus HC studies (1120 LBD patients, 1342 HC) and 68 RBD versus HC studies (1135 RBD patients, 1291 HC) confirmed that both patient groups are significantly impaired relative to healthy controls across all conventionality levels. Hemispheric contributions to figurative language comprehension are dynamic and conventionality-dependent. The left hemisphere is particularly crucial for highly conventionalized expressions, while both hemispheres contribute to novel expressions. These findings are further qualified by methodological moderators: task type and sample size significantly modulated the observed hemispheric differences, whereas aphasia status and number of trials did not. The results have implications for neurocognitive models of figurative language and for the design of clinical assessments, highlighting the need to consider both conventionality and task demands when evaluating figurative language abilities in brain-damaged populations.

results.title: Side-chain effects on solubility, chemical stability, and bioactivation of propofol ester prodrugs
results.journal: European journal of pharmaceutics and biopharmaceutics : official journal of Arbeitsgemeinschaft fur Pharmazeutische Verfahrenstechnik e.V
results.abstract: Propofol is a widely used intravenous anesthetic, but its extremely low aqueous solubility requires lipid-based formulations associated with pharmaceutical limitations. This study aimed to investigate how side-chain structure influences the aqueous solubility, chemical stability, and esterase-mediated bioactivation of propofol ester prodrugs. Thirteen amino acid and dicarboxylate ester derivatives of propofol were synthesized and evaluated for aqueous solubility, chemical stability in phosphate buffer, and metabolic conversion in 50 % human plasma and human liver microsomes (HLM). Selected compounds were further examined by inhibitor studies and time-dependent NMR analysis. All prodrugs exhibited markedly improved aqueous solubility compared with propofol, and five derivatives exhibited propofol-equivalent solubilities exceeding the practical benchmark of 10 mg/mL used in this study. Most compounds remained chemically stable in phosphate buffer at pH 7.0, whereas succinate-, aspartate-, and γ-aminobutyric acid-derived esters showed partial non-enzymatic degradation. Time-dependent NMR analysis suggested that the instability of the succinate derivative was associated with intramolecular cyclization. Distinct side-chain-dependent differences were also observed in esterase-mediated activation. Valine- and γ-aminobutyric acid-derived esters underwent relatively rapid conversion in human plasma, whereas the phenylalanine derivative showed the highest metabolic conversion in HLM. Hydrolysis of the phenylalanine ester in HLM was strongly inhibited by bis-p-nitrophenyl phosphate (BNPP), indicating substantial involvement of carboxylesterases in the activation process. These results demonstrate that side-chain structure strongly influences the balance among aqueous solubility, chemical stability, and esterase-mediated bioactivation of propofol ester prodrugs. The present study provides useful structure-property relationships for the design and evaluation of water-soluble ester prodrugs.

results.title: The Conventional Cost-Effectiveness and Distributional Cost-Effectiveness of Semaglutide for Obesity Treatment
results.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the conventional and distributional cost-effectiveness of semaglutide, laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG), and a "do nothing" option in Black and White racial subgroups. A Markov simulation model was developed from a healthcare perspective over a 25-year time horizon for Black and White adults, aged 65-70, with BMI ≥ 35 and cardiovascular disease. Three interventions were modeled: semaglutide 2.4 mg, LSG, and "do nothing." Semaglutide and LSG interventions are cost-effective compared to a "do nothing" strategy (ICERs = $7300/QALY and $12,100/QALY, respectively). Compared to semaglutide, LSG is more expensive but cost-effective (ICER = $53,700/QALY). Semaglutide is more equitable but is not distributionally cost-effective compared to LSG, because it has a lower EDE within our defined inequality aversion (ε) range. Across 10,000 probabilistic iterations, LSG has a 57% probability and semaglutide has a 43% probability of being the most cost-effective at the willingness-to-pay threshold of $100,000/QALY. Semaglutide becomes distributionally cost-effective when ε ≥ 14.72, where equity impacts of semaglutide outweigh the conventional cost-effectiveness outcomes. LSG is the most conventionally cost-effective treatment option with some uncertainty. Semaglutide is marginally more equitable than LSG but is not a distributionally cost-effective strategy.

results.title: Comparison of Drug-Coated Versus Conventional Balloons for the Side Branches of Bifurcation Lesions: OCVC-BIF Study
results.abstract: Coronary bifurcation lesions remain one of the most challenging lesions. In particular, satisfactory clinical outcomes have not yet been achieved for side branches. The use of drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has demonstrated acceptable clinical outcomes in native coronary arteries. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of additional DCB inflation in the side branches of bifurcation lesions. The OCVC-BIF study (Comparison of Drug-Coated Versus Conventional Balloons for the Side Branch of Bifurcation Lesions) was conducted as a multicenter, randomized, open-label trial. Patients with bifurcation lesions scheduled for drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation in the main vessel followed by kissing balloon inflation were enrolled in the study. The patients were randomized to receive either additional dilatation of the side branch using a DCB after DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation (DCB group) or only DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation using conventional balloons (non-DCB group). The primary end point was restenosis of the side branch, assessed using scheduled coronary angiography at 9 months or symptom-driven coronary angiography during the 1-year follow-up. Restenosis was defined as ≥50% stenosis of the side branch, determined using 3-dimensional bifurcation quantitative coronary angiography. The key secondary end points included major adverse cardiac events at 12 months, which were defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, clinically driven target lesion revascularization, and stent thrombosis. In total, 299 patients were randomized into the DCB (151 patients) and non-DCB (148 patients) groups between October 2019 and September 2024. Serial 3-dimensional bifurcation quantitative coronary angiography evaluation was performed in 262 (87.6%) patients. The restenosis rate was lower in the DCB group than that in the non-DCB group (8.1% versus 18.3%, P=0.012). However, the incidence of major adverse cardiac events at 12 months was similar between them (10.1% versus 12.4%, P=0.58). Additional DCB inflation in the side branch after main-vessel DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation decreases restenosis in the side branch in the treatment of bifurcation lesions. results.title: Upper-extremity Injuries from Side-by-side All-terrain Vehicle Accidents: Experience and Outcomes in over 200 Patients
results.journal: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
results.abstract: Side-by-side all-terrain vehicle (ATV) crashes produce high-energy upper-extremity trauma requiring complex reconstruction. Despite the increasing prevalence of these injuries, characterization of injury patterns, management, and outcomes remains limited. A multicenter retrospective review was performed across 9 level I trauma centers from 2019 to 2023. Adult patients with upper-extremity injuries from side-by-side ATV crashes who were evaluated by the hand surgery service were identified through a trauma registry and manual chart review. Demographics, injury characteristics, operative interventions, and outcomes were collected. A minimum of 6 weeks of follow-up was required for inclusion in the outcome analysis. Among 207 patients (mean age, 32 ± 17 y; 70.5% male), the hand was the most frequently injured region (76.8%), followed by the wrist (30.4%) and forearm (26.6%). Open fractures occurred in 66.7% of patients, including 28% with Gustilo type IIIB or IIIC injuries. Patients underwent a mean of 1.5 operations during the index hospitalization; reconstruction included rotation flaps (10%), free flaps (4%), and dermal substitute placement (27%). Early amputation occurred in 18.4%. At a mean follow-up of 31 weeks (n = 158, 76.3%), patients underwent a mean of 2.6 ± 2.3 total operations; infection occurred in 19.6%; 15.2% required operative debridement; and late amputation occurred in 9.5%, yielding an overall amputation rate of 25.6%. Side-by-side ATV crashes cause severe, often contaminated, multitissue upper-extremity injuries with high rates of infection and amputation despite aggressive surgical management.

results.title: CPAK classification shows limited side-to-side agreement and limited reliability as a standalone surrogate for constitutional alignment in rheumatoid arthritis knees
results.abstract: The Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee classification estimates constitutional coronal alignment. In rheumatoid arthritis knees, disease-related structural changes may affect the bony parameters used for this classification. This study described its distribution and side-to-side agreement in rheumatoid arthritis knees and explored radiographic differences associated with discordance. This single-centre retrospective study included 57 patients and 93 knees treated with unilateral or bilateral total knee arthroplasty for rheumatoid arthritis between January 2014 and December 2024. Classification type was determined from preoperative standing full-length anteroposterior radiographs. Side-to-side agreement was assessed in 36 bilaterally evaluable patients using complete agreement and unweighted Cohen's κ. Side-to-side differences in the medial proximal tibial angle (MPTA), lateral distal femoral angle (LDFA), joint line convergence angle (JLCA) and Larsen score were compared between agreement and discordance groups. In 93 knees, Type I was most frequent at 36.6% (34 of 93), followed by Type II at 25.8% (24 of 93) and Type III at 24.7% (23 of 93). Types VII-IX were not observed. Complete side-to-side agreement was 36.1% (13 of 36), and unweighted Cohen's κ was 0.152 (95% confidence interval, -0.050 to 0.356; p = 0.093). Side-to-side differences in the MPTA, LDFA and JLCA did not differ significantly between groups. A Larsen score difference of at least 1 was more frequent in the discordance group than in the agreement group (78.3% [18 of 23] vs. 38.5% [5 of 13]; p = 0.030), with an odds ratio of 5.760 (95% confidence interval, 1.290-25.640). The classification showed limited side-to-side agreement in rheumatoid arthritis knees, and discordance was associated with asymmetric radiographic structural damage, indicating limited reliability as a standalone surrogate for constitutional alignment or contralateral knee morphology. Level IV.
